---
title: "Consensus and leader election"
---

*Sample chapter for the proposed course plan.*

## Learning outcome

Explain the role of a majority in a three-node consensus group.

**Prerequisites:** Lectures 05–06.

## Core idea

Consensus lets participating nodes agree on decisions despite some failures. In Raft, a three-node group uses a majority of two. A node isolated from the other two cannot commit a new log entry by itself. See Ongaro and Ousterhout, [Raft](https://raft.github.io/raft.pdf), sections 2 and 5.

## Worked scenario

Three registration metadata nodes split into a connected pair and one isolated node. The pair can make progress once a suitable leader is established.

## Discussion

Why should the isolated node avoid accepting independent committed updates?

## Recap

Agreement and progress are separate properties; a partition can prevent progress for some nodes.
